passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
The choirmaster led music in worship.
This psalm is for public worship.

passages.text: I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David waited patiently for the LORD.
The LORD turned toward David.
The LORD listened to David’s cry.
passages.original: לַ֝מְנַצֵּ֗חַ לְדָוִ֥ד מִזְמֽוֹר׃ קַוֺּ֣ה קִוִּ֣יתִי יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥ט אֵ֝לַ֗י וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע שַׁוְעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David spoke to the LORD.
The LORD lifted David up.
David was in a pit of despair.
The LORD brought David out of the miry clay.
The LORD set David’s feet on a rock.
The LORD made David’s steps firm.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲלֵ֤נִי׀ מִבּ֥וֹר שָׁאוֹן֮ מִטִּ֪יט הַיָּ֫וֵ֥ן וַיָּ֖קֶם עַל־ סֶ֥לַע רַגְלַ֗י כּוֹנֵ֥ן אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃

passages.text: He put a new song in my mouth, a hymn of praise to our God. Many will see and fear and put their trust in the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks about God.
God gave me a new song.
This song is a song of praise to our God.
Many people will see what God has done.
Many people will feel awe.
Many people will put their trust in the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֬ן בְּפִ֨י׀ שִׁ֥יר חָדָשׁ֮ תְּהִלָּ֪ה לֵֽאלֹ֫הֵ֥ינוּ יִרְא֣וּ רַבִּ֣ים וְיִירָ֑אוּ וְ֝יִבְטְח֗וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Blessed is the man who has made the LORD his trust, who has not turned to the proud, nor to those who lapse into falsehood.
passages.sermon:
A man trusts in the LORD.
This man is blessed.
He does not turn to proud people.
He does not join those who follow lies.
passages.original: אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי הַגֶּ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁר־ שָׂ֣ם יְ֭הֹוָה מִבְטַח֑וֹ וְֽלֹא־ פָנָ֥ה אֶל־ רְ֝הָבִ֗ים וְשָׂטֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃

passages.text: Many, O LORD my God, are the wonders You have done, and the plans You have for us— none can compare to You— if I proclaim and declare them, they are more than I can count.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is my God.
The LORD has done many wonders.
The LORD has made many plans for us.
No one can compare to the LORD.
If I try to tell about all the LORD’s wonders, I cannot count them all.
If I try to speak about all the LORD’s plans, they are too many for me to declare.
passages.original: רַבּ֤וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתָ׀ אַתָּ֤ה׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַי֮ נִֽפְלְאֹתֶ֥יךָ וּמַחְשְׁבֹתֶ֗יךָ אֵ֫לֵ֥ינוּ אֵ֤ין׀ עֲרֹ֬ךְ אֵלֶ֗יךָ אַגִּ֥ידָה וַאֲדַבֵּ֑רָה עָ֝צְמ֗וּ מִסַּפֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but my ears You have opened. Burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not require.
passages.sermon:
God did not desire sacrifice.
God did not desire offering.
God opened my ears.
God did not require burnt offerings.
God did not require sin offerings.
passages.original: זֶ֤בַח וּמִנְחָ֨ה׀ לֹֽא־ חָפַ֗צְתָּ אָ֭זְנַיִם כָּרִ֣יתָ לִּ֑י עוֹלָ֥ה וַ֝חֲטָאָ֗ה לֹ֣א שָׁאָֽלְתָּ׃

passages.text: Then I said, “Here I am, I have come— it is written about me in the scroll: I delight to do Your will, O my God; Your law is within my heart.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a servant of God.
The speaker responds to God.
The speaker says, "Here I am."
The speaker has come before God.
The scroll contains words about the speaker.
The scroll records the speaker's purpose.
The speaker desires to do God's will.
God is the speaker's God.
The speaker delights in God's will.
God's law is inside the speaker's heart.
passages.original: אָ֣ז אָ֭מַרְתִּי הִנֵּה־ בָ֑אתִי בִּמְגִלַּת־ סֵ֝֗פֶר כָּת֥וּב עָלָֽי׃ לַֽעֲשֽׂוֹת־ רְצוֹנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֣י חָפָ֑צְתִּי וְ֝ת֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ בְּת֣וֹךְ מֵעָֽי׃

passages.text: I proclaim righteousness in the great assembly; behold, I do not seal my lips, as You, O LORD, do know.
passages.sermon:
I speak about righteousness.
I do this in the great assembly.
I do not keep silent.
I do not close my lips.
You, LORD, know this.
passages.original: בִּשַּׂ֤רְתִּי צֶ֨דֶק׀ בְּקָ֘הָ֤ל רָ֗ב הִנֵּ֣ה שְׂ֭פָתַי לֹ֣א אֶכְלָ֑א יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃

passages.text: I have not covered up Your righteousness in my heart; I have declared Your faithfulness and salvation; I have not concealed Your loving devotion and faithfulness from the great assembly.
passages.sermon:
I have not hidden Your righteousness in my heart.
I have spoken about Your faithfulness.
I have declared Your salvation.
I have not concealed Your loving devotion from the great assembly.
I have not concealed Your faithfulness from the great assembly.
passages.original: צִדְקָתְךָ֬ לֹא־ כִסִּ֨יתִי׀ בְּת֬וֹךְ לִבִּ֗י אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ וּתְשׁוּעָתְךָ֣ אָמָ֑רְתִּי לֹא־ כִחַ֥דְתִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ לְקָהָ֥ל רָֽב׃

passages.text: O LORD, do not withhold Your mercy from me; Your loving devotion and faithfulness will always guard me.
passages.sermon:
O LORD, you are merciful.
Do not keep your mercy from me.
Show me your loving devotion.
Show me your faithfulness.
Your loving devotion will guard me always.
Your faithfulness will guard me always.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה לֹא־ תִכְלָ֣א רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ תָּמִ֥יד יִצְּרֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: For evils without number surround me; my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed within me.
passages.sermon:
Many evils surround me.
I cannot count them.
My sins have overtaken me.
I cannot see because of them.
My sins are more than the hairs on my head.
My heart has failed within me.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אָפְפ֥וּ־ עָלַ֨י׀ רָע֡וֹת עַד־ אֵ֬ין מִסְפָּ֗ר הִשִּׂיג֣וּנִי עֲ֭וֺנֹתַי וְלֹא־ יָכֹ֣לְתִּי לִרְא֑וֹת עָצְמ֥וּ מִשַּֽׂעֲר֥וֹת רֹ֝אשִׁ֗י וְלִבִּ֥י עֲזָבָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; hurry, O LORD, to help me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker calls to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The speaker asks the LORD to want to save him.
The speaker asks the LORD to deliver him.
The speaker asks the LORD to come quickly.
The speaker asks the LORD to help him.
passages.original: רְצֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְהַצִּילֵ֑נִי יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָׁה׃

passages.text: May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.
passages.sermon:
Some people want to harm me.
They seek my life.
They wish evil for me.
May these people feel shame.
May they be confused.
May they turn back.
May they be humiliated.
passages.original: יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּר֨וּ׀ יַחַד֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י לִסְפּ֫וֹתָ֥הּ יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָ֭חוֹר וְיִכָּלְמ֑וּ חֲ֝פֵצֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: May those who say to me, “Aha, aha!” be appalled at their own shame.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David prayed to God.
Some people mocked David.
They said to David, “Aha, aha!”
David asked God to judge these people.
David wanted these mockers to feel shame.
David wanted them to be shocked by their own disgrace.
passages.original: יָ֭שֹׁמּוּ עַל־ עֵ֣קֶב בָּשְׁתָּ֑ם הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לִ֝֗י הֶ֘אָ֥ח׀ הֶאָֽח׃

passages.text: May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “The LORD be magnified!”
passages.sermon:
All people who seek God should rejoice in God.
All people who seek God should be glad in God.
People who love God's salvation should always say this.
They should say, "The LORD is great."
They should say, "The LORD be magnified."
passages.original: יָ֘שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ׀ בְּךָ֗ כָּֽל־ מְבַ֫קְשֶׁ֥יךָ יֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה אֹֽ֝הֲבֵ֗י תְּשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my helper and deliverer; O my God, do not delay.
passages.sermon:
I am poor.
I am needy.
The Lord is my helper.
The Lord is my deliverer.
I ask the Lord to remember me.
I ask my God not to delay.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֲדֹנָ֪י יַחֲשָׁ֫ב לִ֥י עֶזְרָתִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־ תְּאַחַֽר׃
